items.quote: What man soever there be of the house of Israel, that killeth an ox, or lamb, or goat, in the camp, or that killeth it out of the camp, 17:4 And bringeth it not unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, to offer an offering unto the LORD before the tabernacle of the LORD; blood shall be imputed unto that man; he hath shed blood; and that man shall be cut off from among his people
items.claim: The text says that any Israelite who kills an ox, lamb, or goat, whether inside or outside the camp, must bring it to the door of the tabernacle as an offering. Anyone who doesn't is counted guilty of shedding blood and is to be cut off from his people.
items.action: requires slaughtered livestock to be brought to the tabernacle as an offering; punishes failure with blood-guilt and being cut off
items.object: ox, lamb, or goat killed in or out of the camp
items.place: the camp; door of the tabernacle of the congregation
items.mechanism: treating slaughter away from the tabernacle as bloodshed and punishing it by cutting the person off from the community

items.quote: To the end that the children of Israel may bring their sacrifices, which they offer in the open field, even that they may bring them unto the LORD, unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, unto the priest, and offer them for peace offerings unto the LORD.
items.claim: The stated purpose of the rule is to move sacrifices that Israelites were making in the open field to the tabernacle door, where they are handed to the priest and offered as peace offerings.
items.action: bring sacrifices to the priest at the tabernacle instead of offering them in the open field
items.place: open field; door of the tabernacle of the congregation
items.mechanism: placing sacrifice under the priest's control at a single sanctuary

items.quote: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, 17:2 Speak unto Aaron, and unto his sons, and unto all the children of Israel, and say unto them; This is the thing which the LORD hath commanded
items.claim: The text presents the command as coming from the LORD to Moses, who is to pass it on to Aaron, his sons, and all the children of Israel.
items.action: issues and passes on a command
items.object: Aaron, his sons, and all the children of Israel
items.mechanism: divine speech relayed by Moses to the priests and the people
